title: Speed Limits for Goods Vehicles
whatItIs: Lorries have lower limits than cars. Over 7.5 tonnes in England and Wales: 50 mph on single carriageways and 60 mph on dual carriageways and motorways. Scotland is lower.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT go over the speed limit for the road, or the limit for your vehicle.

keyFacts: Over 7.5 t (England and Wales): 50 mph single carriageway, 60 mph dual carriageway and motorway.
Up to 7.5 t: 70 mph on motorways, but 60 mph if articulated or towing a trailer.

keyFacts.text: Goods vehicles over 7.5 t MUST NOT use the right-hand lane of a motorway with 3 or more lanes.
Goods vehicles over 12 t first used from 1988, or over 3.5 t from 2005, MUST be speed-limited to 90 km/h.

keyFacts: A limit is a maximum, not a target: slow down for hazards, bad weather and at night.

visual.caption: National speed limits for goods vehicles in mph (Highway Code rule 124)

notes: Maximum laden weight. Built-up areas in Wales: 20 mph. Signs may set lower limits.

a.label: Goods vehicle up to 7.5 t
points: Motorway: 70 mph, or 60 mph if articulated or towing
Needs a speed limiter (over 3.5 t)? No right-hand lane on 3+ lanes

b.label: Goods vehicle over 7.5 t
points: No right-hand lane on 3+ lane motorways (except prescribed cases)

onTheTest.question: You are driving a lorry over 7.5 tonnes on a dual carriageway in England. What is the national speed limit?
onTheTest.why: Rule 124: goods vehicles over 7.5 tonnes in England and Wales are limited to 60 mph on dual carriageways (50 mph in Scotland).

onTheTest.question: You are driving a goods vehicle over 7.5 tonnes on a three-lane motorway. Which lane MUST you not use, except in prescribed circumstances?
onTheTest.why: Rule 265: goods vehicles over 7.5 tonnes, and any vehicle towing a trailer, MUST NOT use the right-hand lane of a 3+ lane motorway.

traps: Over 7.5 t, the motorway limit is 60 mph, not 70.
Up to 7.5 t but articulated or towing? The motorway limit is 60 mph, not 70.
Towing a trailer? The right-hand lane of a 3+ lane motorway is banned too.

jurisdictionNotes.text: Goods vehicles over 7.5 t: 40 mph on single carriageways and 50 mph on dual carriageways. Motorways: 60 mph.
20 mph generally applies on roads with street lights (not motorways), unless signs show otherwise.
